fixed.summary: A terrain layer's normal map (a `kind normal` texture, or a layer of `layerNormals`) is lit correctly on adapters that hold normal maps as two channels (BC5 on desktop GPUs, EAC RG11 on mobile). The terrain shader read the missing z as stored instead of rebuilding it from x and y as materials do, so a layer's normal pointed into the ground and, with antiTiling, every hexagon's slope came out twenty times too steep: black and lit patches over the whole terrain, a honeycomb on snow, and the same patches on a lake's bed seen through shallow og.Water.

A layer normal map whose normals lean one way on average (a scanned map that kept its capture's tilt, such as Poly Haven's snow_02 at 13 degrees) no longer draws lighter and darker hexagons under antiTiling: the map's mean slope, read from its smallest mip, is taken out before each hexagon turns its copy. A map without that lean draws as before; antiTiling 0 keeps showing the texture's own repeat.
